tools.name: get_quote
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants a non-binding estimate for a specific plumbing issue. Returns a price range, typical duration, and next step. Do not present the range as a guaranteed repair price; final pricing is confirmed on-site before work begins.

tools.name: emergency_help
tools.description: Use this immediately when the user describes an urgent plumbing safety or damage situation. Give bounded mitigation guidance and direct them to call Johnson Bros.; for gas, fire, or immediate danger, direct them to leave and call 911 first. tools.name: get_availability
tools.description: Use this when the user wants live Johnson Bros. appointment availability. Returns customer-facing arrival windows and capacity only, never customer data. Do not use it to promise or create an appointment; use request_booking and confirm_booking for that.

tools.name: check_service_area
tools.description: Use this when the user gives a Massachusetts ZIP code or town and wants to know whether Johnson Bros. serves it. Do not use this as proof that a specific appointment is available.

tools.name: get_services_pricing
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to browse Johnson Bros. services or general non-binding price ranges. Do not use it for an issue-specific estimate; use get_quote. Final pricing is confirmed on-site before work begins.

tools.name: business_info
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about Johnson Bros. contact details, credentials, hours, payment methods, service area, or booking process. Do not use it for live availability or a customer-specific record.

tools.name: request_callback
tools.description: Use this only after the user explicitly asks Johnson Bros. to call them about a plumbing need and provides their own contact details. This creates a callback lead, not an appointment. Do not use it for emergency dispatch; tell emergency users to call (617) 479-9911.

tools.name: request_booking
tools.description: Use this only after the user explicitly asks to start a Johnson Bros. booking and confirms their own contact details, service address, issue, and preferred windows. It sends a six-digit SMS code and does not schedule a visit. Do not claim an appointment exists until confirm_booking returns status:co

tools.name: confirm_booking
tools.description: Use this after the customer supplies the six-digit SMS code from request_booking. Only status:confirmed with booked:true means the visit is scheduled. status:callback_pending with booked:false means the office must follow up and must never be described as an appointment. Replaying the same valid con

tools.name: search
tools.description: Use this to find Johnson Bros. Plumbing pages about services, service area, pricing policy, or common questions. Returns ids, titles and URLs only -- call fetch with an id to read the full text. Do not use it to check live appointment availability (use get_availability) or to look up a customer.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Use this to read the full text of a document returned by search. Takes the exact id from a search result. Returns public business information only -- it never returns customer records.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "emergency_help" stacks urgency/override words (important, urgent, immediately, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "business_info" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "confirm_booking" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_quote, get_services_pricing, search · Private data: business_info, request_callback, request_booking, fetch · Public sink: get_quote, request_booking, confirm_booking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_quote, get_services_pricing, search · Private data: business_info, request_callback, request_booking, fetch · Public sink: get_quote, request_booking, confirm_booking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
